items.name: First screen
items.reason: The headline gives the trade: Atlas-L is 2.96 points higher on overall quality at 2.4 times the cost, and the two cheaper models lapse on policy. The decision block gives the lean (Atlas-M), the two prices where the answer flips ($11.09 and $22.05 per point, matching price.atlas-m.atlas-l.overall.per_point_low_unpaired and _high_unpaired), the main risk (the unnamed pass-or-fail judge) and who makes the call. The first claim, price-frontier, prices both steps. One snag: the first confidence bullet says a point worth more than $11.09 'moves the pick off Atlas-M', but the decision block says the run doesn't settle the pick between $11.09 and $22.05.

items.name: Coherent story
items.reason: Each claim matches its values table row by row. In atlas-l-lead, Atlas-L's lead is clear of zero in four tasks, and the speculation bait interval (-1.5 to +3.5) is the stated exception. In cheap-lapses, every cheaper-model interval sits clear of Atlas-M's: Brisk-S on declining speculation is 17 points behind (interval +10.3 to +23.7), and Open-70B on confirming account changes is 81% against 98%. In atlas-parity every Atlas pair overlaps. The pooled frontier (84.7, 89.83, 92.79) reproduces both step prices and puts Open-70B off the frontier. Nothing contradicts the headline.

items.name: Honest emphasis
items.reason: Atlas-M's quality gap to Atlas-L, its weakest task (troubleshooting, -5) and Atlas-L's slower tail all show. But the confidence is 'High' while the lean rests on things nothing declared: a price per point, policy floors that don't exist, and pass-or-fail rates from an undescribed judge. The judge caveat appears in Watch but not in the confidence bullets. The lean also says Atlas-M 'holds every policy behaviour at Atlas-L's level'. What atlas-parity actually shows is 'not told apart'. For example, on confirming account changes the Atlas-L minus Atlas-M interval runs from -2.8 to +2.8 points, so a shortfall of up to about 3 points is not ruled out.

items.name: Sound elision
items.reason: No omission changes the pick among the measured options. Open-70B is off the frontier (a point from Brisk-S to Open-70B costs $6.96; from Open-70B to Atlas-M, $4.58), and the cheaper models' other behaviours trail too. One omission does bear on the routed-mix next step. In persona small talk Open-70B's overall quality is 90, against 88 for Atlas-M (difference -0.1 to +4.1) and 91 for Atlas-L. Its staying-in-character rate is the highest of the four, at 97%. It costs $6.40 per thousand there, against $17.00 for Atlas-M. And no policy behaviour is tested in that task. So the reason given ('it lapses elsewhere') doesn't rule it out as a route.

items.name: Confounds handled
items.reason: Four confounds are each carried. No control: every interval is read unpaired, and the page says pairing would narrow intervals rather than reverse a direction. The undescribed judge: flagged on cheap-lapses and atlas-parity, named in Watch, and given a next step to calibrate it. Nothing declared: the lean is labelled as the analyst's own, with a declaration as the next step. Best of several candidates: stated with its direction. The 9 s latency bar is a separate problem, under item 7.

items.name: Actionable next steps
items.reason: Each step names an action and what it would settle. Declaring a price per point plus floors makes the frontier name one option. A routed mix, run on the same cases, prices a mix nobody has measured. Calibrating the pass-or-fail judge tests whether the lapses and the parity hold. Declaring monthly volume turns per-point prices into a budget figure.

items.name: Evidence fits claims
items.reason: price-frontier says 'Open-70B is the best buy at no price', but its block has only the two frontier steps, so nothing on the page supports that part. The atlas-l-lead caption says 'overall and in each place', but the block has no overall row, and the headline's pooled +2.96 (price.atlas-m.atlas-l.overall.gain) doesn't appear in it. The latency claim and Method cite a '9 s latency bar', but the snapshot declares no criterion at all, and Method itself says nothing was declared.

findings.finding: The sentence says Open-70B is the best buy at no price, but the block draws only the Brisk-S → Atlas-M and Atlas-M → Atlas-L steps. Add Open-70B's two per-point prices: $6.96 from Brisk-S (price.brisk-s.open-70b.overall.per_point) and $4.58 on to Atlas-M (price.open-70b.atlas-m.overall.per_point). Those numbers show why it is passed over at every price. If you'd rather not add them, drop the Open-70B clause from the claim.

The caption says each row is Atlas-L less Atlas-M 'overall and in each place', but the block has only the five task rows. Add the pooled row (+2.96, interval +1.98 to +3.94, from price.atlas-m.atlas-l.overall.gain_interval_unpaired) so the headline's gap sits next to its task breakdown. Otherwise, take 'overall' out of the caption.

The claim and Method both measure latency against 'the 9 s latency bar', but the snapshot declares no criterion of any kind, and Method says nothing was declared. A reader will take 9 s for a declared requirement. Say where 9 s comes from and label it as such (for example 'a 9 s line we chose, not a declared bar'), or state latency descriptively. Atlas-L's p95 tops out at 4.86 s on research questions, against 2.84 s for Atlas-M.

Fix the first confidence bullet: 'values a point of overall quality above $11.09 … moves the pick off Atlas-M' contradicts the decision block, which says the run doesn't settle the pick between $11.09 and $22.05. Write it as 'above $11.09 the pick is unsettled, and above $22.05 it moves to Atlas-L'. Separately, the confidence line says 'High' while the exclusion of the cheaper models rests entirely on pass-or-fail rates from an undescribed judge, and that caveat is missing from the confidence bullets. Add it there, or lower the stated confidence.

In the lean, 'It holds every policy behaviour at Atlas-L's level' claims more than atlas-parity shows, which is only that the two can't be told apart. Each difference interval still allows a gap of about 3 points (on confirming account changes, -2.8 to +2.8). Reword to 'is not told apart from Atlas-L on any policy behaviour'.

Widen the routed-mix next step. In persona small talk, Open-70B can't be told apart from Atlas-M on overall quality (90 against 88, difference -0.1 to +4.1). It has the highest staying-in-character rate (97%), costs $6.40 against $17.00 per thousand there, and that task tests no policy behaviour. Add Open-70B on persona small talk as a route to price beside Atlas-L on troubleshooting. Also revise the omitted-item reason that says it 'changes no option a decider would weigh'.
